title: Uptime partnerships action catalog — cross-team reliability accelerator (Q3 2026)
content:
Status: working draft for review by oncall leads, infra, product platform (please add TODOs inline).

One-line summary:
This document collects the high-impact cross-team actions, ownership, and phased milestones for the Reliability Accelerator focused on SLO adoption and measurable uptime improvements for core inference surfaces (hosted API + Dedicated routing) in Q3 2026.

Goals (what success looks like by end of Q3):
- 90% of critical services have at least one SLO defined, instrumented, and onboarded to the SRE dashboard.
- Observable reduction in P95 tail latency for model serve endpoints by 15% for interactive workloads (measured vs. 2026-05 baseline).
- Defined and tested escalation flow across product, infra, and incident response for SLO breaches.
- Two customers piloting Dedicated failover policies for degraded capacity scenarios.

Scope / primary surfaces (in priority order):
1) Hosted API (frontend, inference routing, model cache layer)
2) Dedicated control plane + GPU pool scheduler
3) Model-variant router and fallback chains
4) Console routes for rollout (per-route dashboards + rollout hooks)

Outcomes / deliverables (artifact-oriented):
- SLO catalog spreadsheet row per service (SLO id, owner, target, measurement signal, alert thresholds).
- Telemetry ingestion pipelines configured for p50/p95/p99, error-rate, availability, and request volume.
- Runbook snippet + escalation map for service-level SLO breaches.
- Pilot checklist and retro template.

Stakeholders & roles (high-level):
- SRE lead: Ava Chen (program owner) — overall timetable, SLO governance, runbook signoff.
- Infra: Diego Martinez — metrics pipeline, exporter changes, sampling policies.
- Serving runtime: Priya Nair — model router instrumentation, latency buckets, canary hooks.
- Product / Console: Jordan Park — dashboard templates, rollout UX for SLO targets.
- Solutions / CS: Maya Singh — coordinate pilot customers and measure business impact.
- Oncall rotation: rotation leads (see TODO: insert names) — participate in tabletop and validate alerts.

Phased plan (milestone-oriented):
- Discovery (Week 0–2): baseline measurement, gap analysis, small survey to service owners (SRE-312). Deliverable: SLO candidate list.
- Quick wins (Week 2–6): wire up missing exporters, add 1–2 telemetry metrics per service, create dashboard template. Deliverable: 10 services with dashboards and measurement.
- Pilot (Week 6–10): pick 3 critical services, run canary rollouts with SLO-based alerts, exercise escalation path in a tabletop. Deliverable: pilot retro + adjustment list.
- Rollout (Week 10–14): scale to additional services, bake alerts into oncall rotation, automate basic remediation (circuit-breakers / fallback to cheap model). Deliverable: SLOs enforced by alerts for majority of critical lanes.

SLO taxonomy (recommended default patterns):
- Availability SLO: successful-response-rate over rolling 7d window. Typical target: 99.9 (for control-plane), 99.5 (for non-critical batch).
- Latency SLO: p95 latency per request type (chat vs. generation vs. embeddings) over rolling 7d window. Start with target = current baseline * 1.05 to avoid noisy churn during adoption.
- Error-rate SLO: 5xx+client errors per 1000 requests over 24h.
- Quality guardrail (soft SLO): model fallback rate when quantized variant used; track and alert on > X% fallbacks.

Measurement & instrumentation notes: (Infra / Serving runtime action items)
- Ensure request-level tracing includes route_id, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, tenant_id (PII-free).
- Tag metrics with deployment ring (canary/stable), region, and capacity tier.
- Add p95 latency histograms at the edge and at model execution boundary (separate signals).
- Sampling: preserve 100% metadata for errors; sample regular requests at 10% if ingestion budget constrained (INFRA-205 to change sampling rules).

Alerting & remediation patterns:
- Severity 1: SLO breach for > 30m for a core route -> page oncall SRE + product triage.
- Severity 2: rapidly rising p95 for > 60m -> alert to infra + autoscaling ops.
- Auto-remediation candidates: route-level fallback to smaller model, enable caching layer, scale replicaset. These should be feature-flagged and throttled.

Pilot checklist (for each service):
- SLO defined and documented in catalog (owner assigned).
- Metrics streaming to observability (test queries return expected numbers).
- Dashboard template created and shared with product owner.
- Alert rule created and tested in staging with synthetic traffic.
- Tabletop run completed with >=2 simulated breach scenarios.
- Post-pilot retro and action items tracked in JIRA.

Governance & cadence:
- Weekly sync (30m) — SRE leads + infra + product - standing agenda: progress, blockers, top 3 risks.
- Biweekly executive check-in (15m) — summarized metrics and high-impact decisions.
- Quarterly SLO review — re-evaluate targets after 90d.

Communications plan:
- Launch note for each phase: slack post in #eng-ops and #sre with summary and leads.
- Confluence page (linked) will be the canonical SLO catalog and how-to.
- Customer pilot updates: shared weekly to CS stakeholders and customer success manager.

Dependencies & known blockers:
- Observability retention and ingest cost caps (finance approval needed to raise for pilot).
- Serving runtime instrumentation gaps for sequence-length buckets (work in Priya's backlog).
- Dedicated scheduling telemetry needs small agent change (JIRA-INFRA-205).

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Alert fatigue if thresholds set too aggressively -> Mitigation: tiered alerts, use temporary hold windows during rollout.
- Risk: Oncall burn during pilot -> Mitigation: limit pilot to fixed hours, staff with extra rotation resources.
- Risk: Data privacy constraints for tenant tags -> Mitigation: use hashed tenant ids and conform to privacy review (security signoff required).

Success metrics (to track weekly):
- percent_critical_services_with_SLO = (# services with SLO / total critical services)
- delta_p95_latency_vs_baseline (percentage)
- # of SLO-related pages per week (should trend down post-mitigation)
- pilot_customer_satisfaction (qualitative)

Open questions / decisions needed (please add inline):
- What is the canonical list of "critical services"? (propose: api-gateway, model-router, kv-cache, scheduler, console-route)
- Agree to default SLO windows (7d vs 28d)
- Finance approval: temporary increase in metric ingest for pilot (owner: finance ops)

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Owner (Ava): finalize SLO candidate list and tag owners (due 2026-06-19).
- Diego: prototype exporter change for sequence-length tags in staging (due 2026-06-22).
- Priya: add p95 histograms to model execution boundary in dev cluster (due 2026-06-24).
- Jordan: build dashboard template and add example for one service (due 2026-06-24).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive — we want concrete, small wins that unblock teams. Please call out any misses in scope (e.g., do we need legal signoff for telemetry changes?).

Appendix: helpful links and references
- Proto SLO catalog (sheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ExampleSLOCatalog
- Incident playbook template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/incident-playbook-template
- Telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config/pull/128

End of draft.
